judge.summary: The patient successfully scheduled an appointment for knee pain with Dr. Emily Chen. The agent correctly identified the specialist, confirmed the appointment details, and provided instructions for the first visit. The call concluded naturally after all necessary information was exchanged.

conversation_quality.notes: The conversation flowed well, though there was a slight overlap at the beginning of the patient's second turn.

agent_quality.notes: The agent handled the new patient intake perfectly, including the specific arrival instructions.

technical_quality.notes: The 3.0s of dead air noted in the metrics slightly impacted the pacing.

criteria.criterion: A specific weekday date, time and provider were confirmed back to the patient
criteria.evidence: 00:20: 'I have you scheduled with Dr. Emily Chen on Monday at 9:30 AM.'

criteria.criterion: The agent used the patient's own name and DOB (did not substitute demo values without saying so)
Call ended naturally after the patient said goodbye

hypotheses.hypothesis: Agent states a date of birth the caller never gave (a placeholder such as July fourth 2000) or skips asking for it and uses one on file
Agent fabricates or assigns a placeholder DOB instead of using the one given
Agent confirms a slot without stating the day/time/provider explicitly
Agent asks a new patient for "the phone number on file"
Agent cannot answer "what should I bring" and reaches for a transfer instead

positive_controls: Agent correctly identified Dr. Emily Chen as the appropriate specialist for knee pain (00:10)
Agent provided clear instructions for new patient arrival (00:20)
simulator_notes: The simulator performed well; no improvements needed.
judge.testing_value: This scenario effectively tested the happy-path scheduling flow and the agent's ability to provide accurate clinic policy information.
